spec_basis: STU-TYP-004: Text-on-path: a StudioTextStory with text_kind = path binds to a StudioVectorPath and flows glyphs along it, with editable flow-extent handles (start/end), per-section baseline-distance offset, flow-direction control, side-flip, and reverse-path-direction ... The path is the SAME StudioVectorPath primitive used by the vector domain (14.5); there is no text-only path type.

STU-TYP-120: A path story binds to a StudioVectorPath (geometry owned by 14.5) and stores: start_t and end_t (position along the path expressed relative to the path's segments), spacing (curve-tightening compensation), flipped (not_flipped | flipped | undefined), and a per-run baseline_offset.

STU-TYP-121: path_type_alignment (top_path | bottom_path | center_path ...), text_type_alignment (ascender | descender | center | baseline | above_right_em_box | below_left_em_box | above_right_icf_box | below_left_icf_box ...). A third enumeration path_effect selects the distortion: rainbow, skew, ribbon, stair_step, gravity. rainbow is the default and rotates each glyph to the path tangent; the other four are shipped, non-optional members.

STU-VEC-038: A StudioVectorPath/StudioVectorNetwork MUST be usable as a typographic baseline (text on a path) ... The vector domain owns only the geometry; the text run, shaping, path-text options and area-type behaviour are owned by the Typography engine (14.7) ... Converting text to outlines produces standard vector geometry.

STU-LAY-023: Text on a path MUST bind a StudioTextStory to a StudioVectorPath ... this is the single Studio text-on-path capability shared with the vector and typography domains and MUST NOT be reimplemented here.
STU-VEC-052: Selection-wide colour editing ... MUST route through the standard command lifecycle so bulk recolour edits are auditable and undoable as one history entry.

STU-VEC-142: four global adjustment sliders (saturation_shift, brightness_shift, temperature_shift, luminosity_shift; soft -100..100, default 0, percent) ... Palette generation, harmony rules and colour reduction are owned by 14.8; the vector domain consumes them and MUST NOT fork a parallel colour model.

STU-COL-235: A DETERMINISTIC harmony primitive generating a variation palette from a base colour under a named rule. Rules: complementary, split_complementary, analogous, monochromatic, triad, tetrad, compound, shades, tints, warm, cool, vivid, muted ... MUST be a pure function of (base colour, rule, count, library).

STU-COL-236: A DETERMINISTIC recolour primitive remapping every colour in a selection. ASSIGN: a table of current-colour to new-colour rows, with merge, exclude, and prominence-weighted extraction that orders rows by area coverage. EDIT: linked colour handles on a wheel, with a global link toggle ... Plus COLOUR REDUCTION: reduce to N colours ... with independent preserve toggles for white, black and greys, and a colorize_method selection. recolor.target_color_count hard_min 1.

STU-VEC-034: Gradient Mesh: Studio MUST support gradient-mesh objects (StudioGradient kind gradient.mesh) -- a grid of mesh points and lines interpolating colour and per-point opacity across a shape -- with add/remove mesh point and line editing and conversion from an existing gradient or shape.
STU-COL-036: a mesh gradient stores an editable grid of mesh points each with color and transparency, interpolating across the patch, and is convertible from a linear/radial gradient.
STU-VEC-059: Every procedural construct in this group (blend, live paint, gradient mesh, ...) MUST persist its live parameters AND its source references as vector authority.

STU-COL-212: Separations preview. Three inspection facets on one surface: per-plate visibility toggles (each ink on or off, plus a composite view); an INK LIMIT view with a configurable total-ink-coverage threshold ...; and a per-ink percentage-coverage readout at a sampled point. All three MUST be readable as structured inspection state, not only as pixels.
STU-COL-020: Spot inks separate, proof, overprint, and appear in the Ink Manager/Separations Preview regardless of any branded library.
